topic: Moving expenses (line 21900): new home at least 40 km closer to the new work location by the shortest public route; deductible only from employment/self-employment income earned at the new location; unused part carries forward to future years (from that income); temporary living (meals and lodging) up to 15 days

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): Riley, new job in 2025; old home 52 km from the new work location (shortest public route); option A 18 km → 34 km closer (fails the 40 km test); option B 9 km → 43 km closer (qualifies). Eligible moving costs $4,200 (truck, travel, temporary living). Started work in December 2025 and earned $2,500 there in 2025 → deducts $2,500 for 2025; $1,700 carried forward against future income at the new location. No employer reimbursement.

sources.rule: canada.ca CRA Line 21900 – Moving expenses (updated Jan 20, 2026): 'your new home must be at least 40 kilometres closer (by the shortest public route) to your new work location' (via Google search excerpts, 2026-11-01)
sources.income: canada.ca CRA line 21900: 'You can deduct eligible moving expenses from the employment or self-employment income you earned at your new work location'; not from other income such as investment income or EI
sources.carry: canada.ca CRA line 21900 / Income Tax Folio S1-F3-C4 ¶4.18: unused moving expenses carried forward and deducted from income earned at the new work location in a future year; no carry back
sources.temp: Income Tax Folio S1-F3-C4 and CRA common adjustments: meals and lodging near the old or new residence for a period not exceeding 15 days
